questions.question: What role should the principles-and-decisions v0.4 doc play in the remote-store repo?

options.label: Research, then RFC (Recommended)
options.description: Commit it as a point-in-time research doc under sdd/research/. A following RFC selects which definitions and criteria become binding and in which existing homes (ADR template, /observe loop, 000-process doc types). Keeps rationale out of authority docs and leaves the text as written.

options.label: Authority doc directly
options.description: Rewrite it into Intent & Scope, Rules, Guides as a sibling of SPEC-DESIGN.md. Fastest to bind, but its rationale and references must move elsewhere, it costs process budget, and it binds before any trial.

options.label: Stays outside the repo
options.description: Keep it in your research repository as a general reference; this repo only links to it. Nothing binds here, and the seven decision homes stay as they are.

questions.question: What should I do next with the v0.4 doc?

options.label: Trial on repo records (Recommended)
options.description: Apply P1 to P7 and D1 to D7 to a small sample (for example CLAUDE.md principles, ADR-0048's decisions, a few OP-01 decisions) and report where the rubric discriminates and where it does not. Report only; tests the doc before anything binds.

options.label: Full review of the text
options.description: A finding-by-finding review of v0.4 itself: definitions, criteria overlap, examples, claims against sources. Improves the doc but does not show whether it works on real records.

options.label: Draft the missing parts
options.description: Propose additions for the three gaps: the boundary between principle, rule, clause and axiom; quality of a collection of decisions; an independence test taken from the axiom method. Extends the doc before it has been tried.

questions.question: What should I do next with the v0.4 doc?
Which part of my read of the principles-and-decisions v0.4 doc do you disagree with?

options.label: Placement came too early
options.description: I asked where the doc lives and what binds before we agreed on what it says and whether my read of it is right. We discuss content first; no repo role is chosen yet.

options.label: Dropping the axiom link
options.description: I withdrew my analogy between axioms and principles after reading the doc. You do see a relation between the axiom work and principles or decisions, and I should not have dropped it.

options.label: The shortfalls list
options.description: One or more of my seven points misreads the doc or judges it against the wrong yardstick, for example measuring a general reference against this repo's specific pains.

options.label: My reading of your goal
options.description: My restatement of what you want (one vocabulary for what a principle and a decision are and how to write them, for this repo) is off, so the whole read aims at the wrong target.

questions.question: To bring the agreed concepts and six principles (foundation first, fixed words, breakable, result not history, say what kind, few and distinct) to everything written in remote-store, what should be written first?

options.label: An RFC for the whole repo (Recommended)
options.description: States the pain with its evidence here, the concepts and principles, which artifact kinds and skills change and how, and how we measure it (prose findings per /ship loop). Nothing binds until you accept it. It is the repo's normal route for a process change and gets a backlog item and trace.

options.label: The doc itself, as a draft
options.description: I draft the repo's own 'principles and decisions: what they are and how to write them' from v0.4 and what we agreed, written in the form it describes. Where it lives and what it binds is decided after you have read it.

options.label: Apply it to the repo's own process first
options.description: Write the foundation of how we work here (terms, a few principles with why and test, how they fit together) from CLAUDE.md's principles and the authority docs. A trial of the method on ourselves before proposing it for everything.

options.label: A map of where we stand
options.description: Report only: each artifact kind in the repo (spec, RFC, ADR, backlog item, skill, record) read against the six principles, with evidence of where it holds and where it breaks. No proposal yet; you decide from the map.

questions.question: remote-store is a public repository, and both source documents come from outside it: your v0.4 reference and the durable-prose problem note, which names sam-services, its audit-009 and its PR numbers. How should the RFC use them?

options.label: Cite, commit nothing external (Recommended)
options.description: The RFC states the concepts and principles in its own words and rests on evidence already in this repo (token-usage report § 5, the OP-01 record, the research records). The two documents are named as unpublished input, with no content from the other repository copied in.

options.label: Commit v0.4 as research
options.description: v0.4 goes into sdd/research/ as a point-in-time record and the RFC links it. Its § 6.3 carries your name and the sam-services references into the public repo unless you give me a cleaned version first.

options.label: Commit both
options.description: v0.4 and the problem note both become research records here. Full provenance in one place, but the other repository's audit, PR numbers and figures become public.

questions.question: What should RFC-0032 propose to bind, once accepted, for durable prose in remote-store?

options.label: New and rewritten work (Recommended)
options.description: The concepts and six principles bind an artifact when it is written or substantially rewritten, the same trigger CONTENT-RULES Rule 7 uses. Existing artifacts stay as they are; what changes per artifact kind is open in the RFC and settled by the map during review.

options.label: Foundations only
options.description: It binds only the foundation of a subject: before detail is written about a subject (the store, the process, a skill), its terms and principles exist. Individual artifacts get no new rule. Smaller and easier to check, but leaves ADRs, backlog items and skills as they are.

options.label: Everything, with a migration
options.description: It binds every durable artifact and the RFC carries a plan to bring existing ones into line. Widest effect and the largest cost, and it commits to extent before the map has shown where the pain is.
